newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy says cost to families of budget exaggerated.
newsitem.headline: Italy says cost to families of budget exaggerated.

text.p: The Italian government said on Sunday the cost to families of the 1997 budget had been exaggerated.
"The truth is that the weight will be somewhere much lower than a milion (lire)," Treasury undersecretary Laura Pennacchi told reporters.

Newspapers had suggested that the package, designed to put Italy's finances into shape for a planned European monetary union in 1999, would cost the average family some one million lire ($658). Pennacchi described as "absolute folly" estimates that the budget would cost families three to four million.
The 62.5 trillion lire budget unveiled on Friday includes plans to to raise 13 trillion lire from a special one-off Euro tax and 12 trillion from so far unspecified treasury operations.
Opposition and business leaders have criticised it for failing to include cuts in pension and healthcare benefits.
